# easy-ping

> Free, open-source notifications for TypeScript. In-app inbox,
> transactional email, web push, mobile push and Telegram. Runs inside your
> app; stores notifications in your own Postgres, MySQL, SQLite or MongoDB
> database. No cloud component, no per-notification billing.

This library shipped after most language models' training cutoffs.
For the full API surface an AI assistant needs to use it correctly,
fetch /llms-full.txt from this same origin.

## Docs

### Getting started

- [Introduction](/docs/introduction): A framework-agnostic, type-safe, self-hosted notifications library for TypeScript.
- [Quickstart](/docs/quickstart): A working inbox, email and push in five files. This walks the Postgres and Drizzle path. MongoDB differs only in step 2.
- [Configuration](/docs/configuration): The full easyPing() option reference.
- [Use with an AI assistant](/docs/ai-assistant): easy-ping shipped after every current model's training cutoff. Here's how to make Cursor or Claude write against the real API instead of an invented one.

### Core

- [send()](/docs/send): The one function that starts a notification. It commits the rows first, and what it waits for after that is the delivery mode's call.
- [Delivery modes](/docs/delivery-modes): Four ways to run providers after send() returns, all sitting on the same cron sweep.
- [Route handler](/docs/route-handler): One export mounts the whole inbox API, plus whatever routes your plugins add.
- [Cron sweep](/docs/cron): The durability floor beneath every delivery mode. Required for cron and deferred, recommended everywhere.

### Channels

- [In-app inbox](/docs/in-app-inbox): Built into core — cursor pagination, a headless React hook, and seen vs. read as genuinely different states.
- [Web push](/docs/web-push): VAPID and aes128gcm on Web Crypto — no node:crypto, so it runs on Workers and Edge, not only Node.
- [Email](/docs/email): A Resend provider ships in the box; the EmailProvider interface is open for any other service.
- [Telegram](/docs/telegram): A bot the user connects with one tap. Messages go to every chat they linked; blocked chats prune themselves.
- [Mobile push](/docs/mobile-push): Native push to iOS and Android through Expo's push service. A token registry, fan-out per device, and receipts that catch uninstalls.

### Plugins

- [Preferences](/docs/preferences): A per-type, per-channel opt-out center with signed unsubscribe links, as a plugin.
- [Digests](/docs/digests): Timezone-aware batching for anyone who set their notification frequency to daily or weekly.
- [Push devices](/docs/push-plugin): The device registry behind the push channel — registration, fan-out, and pruning.
- [Writing a plugin](/docs/writing-a-plugin): The surface preferences, digests and push are all built on — hooks, scoped storage, and a channel of your own.

### Adapters

- [Postgres · any driver](/docs/postgres-adapter): Postgres without an ORM. One function — run a parameterised statement, return rows — is the entire contract.
- [Drizzle · Postgres](/docs/drizzle-adapter): The reference adapter — raw SQL under a Drizzle-shaped schema, with an atomic FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED claim.
- [MongoDB](/docs/mongodb-adapter): The same library, the same conformance suite, no tables — just indexes.
- [MySQL](/docs/mysql-adapter): MySQL 8 or MariaDB through any driver. The same query-function contract as Postgres, plus the row count MySQL needs because it has no RETURNING.
- [SQLite](/docs/sqlite-adapter): SQLite through node:sqlite, better-sqlite3 or anything with the same prepare().all()/run() shape. One writer, so the claim is one UPDATE.
- [Writing an adapter](/docs/writing-an-adapter): The DatabaseAdapter interface, and the conformance suite that proves an implementation actually holds the claim guarantee.

### Guides

- [React Native](/docs/react-native): The same client on a phone: useNotifications from easy-ping/react-native, a live stream through expo/fetch, and native push.
- [Upgrading](/docs/upgrading): What happens to your schema when a new version adds a column, on each database path.
- [When something fails](/docs/failures): Delivery is quiet by design. Here's how to see what actually happened.
- [Security](/docs/security): The trust boundaries the library enforces, and the two things it can't protect you from.
- [Stability and versioning](/docs/stability): What you can build on today without it moving, what may still change before 1.0, and how a change is announced when it does.

### Releases

- [Changelog](/docs/changelog): Every release, what changed in it, and why — including the bugs worth knowing about.
